_doc: Held-out key for T12. The cause is the predicate in the suite: fullMs < emptyMs * 2 + 25 budgets the files' cost as a multiple of the bare spawn time. A fast runner measures a small empty time and gets a tight allowance that one ordinary stall exceeds, while a slow machine's large empty time makes the budget generous, so it never reproduces there. A pass names the suite and matches both groups. A hedged mechanism fails.

groups.why: the budget is a multiple of, or scales with, the empty-inbox spawn time
match: ^(?=[\s\S]*(?:empty|baseline|spawn|startup|start-up|process start))(?=[\s\S]*(?:multipl|\* ?2|\bx ?2\b|\b2 ?x\b|two times|twice|double|scales? with|proportional|relative to|ratio|derived from|depends on|tied to))

groups.why: so a faster machine gets a tighter budget and a slow one a generous budget

cause.mechanism: The flat-cost check allows fullMs < emptyMs * 2 + 25, a budget proportional to the empty spawn cost. A fast runner measures a small empty baseline and so gets a tight allowance that one ordinary 100ms stall exceeds, while a slow Mac's 200ms baseline leaves plenty of room.

The assertion budgets the 25-file cost as twice the empty-inbox time plus 25ms, so the allowance scales with how fast the machine spawns node: the quick macOS runner at 38ms gets a much smaller margin, and a single filesystem hiccup fails it.

Slow machines get a generous limit and fast ones a strict one: the threshold is a multiple of the empty-run baseline, so the 38ms CI Mac allows about 63ms for the files while the 200ms developer Mac allows over 200ms.

fullMs < emptyMs * 2 + 25 grants the 25 files a margin of the empty spawn time plus 25ms. On a slower machine that allowance grows larger, which is why the developer Mac cannot reproduce a 113ms stall that fails the 38ms CI runner.

The predicate fullMs < emptyMs * 2 + 25 budgets a fixed I/O cost as a multiple of an unrelated spawn baseline. A faster machine measures a smaller empty time and therefore gets a TIGHTER absolute allowance, while a slow box's baseline makes the budget generous.

The predicate fullMs < emptyMs * 2 + 25 lets the 25 files cost only emptyMs + 25: the CI Mac spawns in 38ms so the files get 63ms and one 113ms stall fails it, while the dev Mac's 200ms empty time allows 225ms.
The budget is emptyMs * 2 + 25, a multiple of the spawn baseline, so the fast CI Mac at 38ms gets a tight 63ms allowance that one ordinary stall, maybe a GC pause, exceeds.
The macOS CI runners are shared and noisy, so a garbage-collection pause or a disk stall during the 25-file run adds about 100ms and pushes it over the budget.
The hook reads every waiting file's contents instead of only statting it, so 25 files of 4 KB cost over 100ms on the macOS runner's slower disk.
On APFS the first stat of a freshly created file is slow, so listing 25 new files costs about 100ms more than the empty inbox on a fresh CI disk.
The budget is twice the empty baseline plus 25ms, and the 25-file run on macOS takes longer because APFS stats are expensive, so it exceeds that budget.
Fast CI machines leave tight timing, so any 100ms stall during the 25-file run fails the check.
The budget is a multiple of the empty spawn time, so a fast runner gets a tight allowance that one stall exceeds. Possibly the runner is also just noisy.
The budget is emptyMs * 2 + 25, and the CI Mac at 38ms gets 63ms for the files, which a 113ms APFS stat stall exceeds.
